solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink readily available after end of restrictions

indicators.note: the first piece is placed after the end letter, so that letter comes first
the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from restrictions

parts.note: something handy is close at hand and ready to use

explanation.surface: Once lockdown rules end, a drink is easy to get hold of again.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a pub drink of beer mixed with lemonade, so it is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Step made by the leading character in agitation

indicators.note: the leading character is placed in the word for agitation

parts.note: a stir is a commotion or state of agitation
the first character of the alphabet is A

explanation.surface: A dance step invented by the star of the show in a nervous frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The leading character' sounds like a lead actor, but it means the first letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a flight of steps, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Sailor leads party chaps exposing belly

indicators.note: the sailor comes at the front of what follows, leading it

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
a do is an informal word for a party
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A seaman heads off to a party where the men take their shirts off and show their stomachs.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the belly, the part of the body holding the stomach; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Transport system held up by poet and young lady

indicators.note: the poet's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the Tube is London's Underground railway system

explanation.surface: A poet and a young woman are delayed by a breakdown on the train network.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the railway backwards. The Tube is London's underground railway; 'held' suggests a delay, but it means contained.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her first formal entrance into fashionable society.

clue.text: Son, little fellow, seen as a pain

parts.note: titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A small boy is regarded as a nuisance by his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'titch' is British informal slang for a very small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side, often brought on by running.

clue.text: Provider of sugar wants an extra bit of sweetness in —–

indicators.note: the bit of sweetness is placed in the sugar company's name

parts.note: Tate (of Tate & Lyle) is a well-known British sugar refiner

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sugar company wants a little more sweetness in something, with the blank to be filled in.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash stands for the answer: Tate wants extra sweetness in its TASTE. Tate & Lyle is a famous British sugar company.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank completes the sentence: sweetness is something experienced through the palate's sense of flavour.

clue.text: Complicated flavour experienced

parts.note: a tang is a sharp, distinctive flavour
to have led a life is to have experienced it

explanation.surface: A seasoned taster finds a flavour hard to pin down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangled means knotted and confused, so a synonym for complicated.

clue.text: Inadequate sort of believer managed church — certainly no help

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, one kind of believer
ran means managed, as in ran a business
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A half-hearted worshipper ran a church badly and was of no use to anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance gets in the way, so it is the opposite of help: an obstacle.

clue.text: What makes Dad be troubled — British company admitting that financial problem

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the company's letters take the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: BT is British Telecom, the UK telephone company

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of Dad be are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something upsets a father, and a phone company is involved in his money worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the letters of 'Dad be'; 'What makes' and 'that' merely link the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad debt is money owed that will never be repaid, a problem for a lender's finances.

clue.text: Like one figure here, very stupid

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
the Roman numeral I is one
nine is a number, or figure

explanation.surface: Someone resembles a figure seen nearby and looks foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means donkey-like, and so silly or foolish.

clue.text: England's fast bowler leading team's attack

indicators.note: the bowler's name goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: Stuart Broad was a long-serving fast bowler for the England cricket team
a side is a team, and the 's is a link

explanation.surface: England's quick bowler spearheads the team's assault on the batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuart Broad was an England fast bowler in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a fierce verbal attack, originally a volley of guns from one side of a ship.

clue.text: Playwright is given small drink — a hint of thirsty desire

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, especially whisky

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its first letter

parts.note: an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: A writer gets a nip of whisky, with a slight thirst still nagging.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramaturge is a writer or adapter of plays, so a playwright.

clue.text: Pullman's young girl stars

definitions.meaning: the girl heroine of Philip Pullman's His Dark Materials novels
a northern constellation containing the bright star Vega

explanation.surface: A novelist's young heroine is the star of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the name: Lyra Belacqua is Pullman's heroine, and Lyra the Lyre is a constellation.

clue.text: Cleric's set of church rules maybe

definitions.meaning: a clergyman attached to a cathedral chapter
a body of ecclesiastical law or principles

explanation.surface: A churchman's rulebook, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is both a cathedral clergyman and a body of rules laid down by the Church.

clue.text: Governmental arrangement — trick taking in a lot, I repeatedly suspect

indicators.note: the trick's letters take the jumbled group inside them

parts.note: a con is a confidence trick

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are scrambled
the letter is used more than once, here twice

explanation.surface: A government pact is just a con, I keep suspecting, drawing in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives two I's; 'suspect' scrambles them with 'a lot' to make OALITI, and 'taking in' puts that inside the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalition is a government formed by an alliance of parties.

clue.text: Beset by stress I had mishap

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the contraction sits inside the word for stress

parts.note: an accent is the stress placed on a syllable
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Under pressure, I had a minor setback.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unplanned unfortunate event, so a mishap.

clue.text: Very well — do better than that, friend!

parts.note: to cap it is to outdo or top what was just done
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone praises a friend's performance but dares them to outdo it.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitally is an old-fashioned word meaning excellently, so very well.

clue.text: Mother takes time with hair — one probably in bedroom?

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Mum takes her time doing her hair, probably sitting in the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the padded base of a bed, so is usually found in a bedroom.

clue.text: Time before a concert with nothing being imbibed in bar

indicators.note: the time letter is placed in front of the rest
to imbibe is to drink in, so the zero goes inside the concert

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Before a concert there is time for a drink-free visit to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous series of summer classical concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A taproom is a room in a pub where beer is served from the tap, a bar.

clue.text: Group led by "star man"

parts.note: a Wild West sheriff wears a star badge and leads a band of deputised men in pursuit of outlaws

explanation.surface: A band fronted by a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star man' suggests a celebrity or the Bowie song, but the star is a sheriff's badge.
explanation.definitionFit: In Westerns a sheriff, the man with the star, gathers armed townsmen into a body to chase outlaws.

clue.text: Colonial who may sort out disagreement?

definitions.meaning: a person who goes to live in a new colony
someone who resolves a dispute, read literally as one who settles

explanation.surface: A colonist who might be called on to resolve a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist makes a new home in a colony; read whimsically, one who settles an argument too.

clue.text: Conclusion of evil and little devil is powerless

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: an imp is a small demon or mischievous child

explanation.surface: The end of evil arrives and a small demon is left helpless.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means slack and lacking strength or force, so weak and powerless.

clue.text: Thought a timid note should be redrafted

indicators.note: redrafting rewrites the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a shy, diffident message ought to be rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Meditation is deep reflection, so the noun thought is a synonym.

clue.text: TV detective a bit short

indicators.note: short means lacking its end, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a morsel is a small bit, especially of food

explanation.surface: A television sleuth who is a little on the small side.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse was the hero of a long-running British TV detective series set in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the ITV series.

clue.text: Horrible to sea captain on dangerous mission

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A captain faces terrible conditions on a perilous voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Lawrence Oates died on Scott's doomed 1912 Antarctic expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Oates walked out into the blizzard on Scott's fatal South Pole expedition.

clue.text: Large attempt to embrace love when bias is evident

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the zero goes between the two words

parts.note: big means large
a try is an attempt
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A big effort at affection when prejudice shows itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is intolerant prejudice, so a strong form of bias.

clue.text: Greek character and female pop singer about to wail

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
Lulu is a Scottish singer famous for Shout

explanation.surface: A Greek and a pop star are about to start howling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ETA + LULU together. Lulu is a long-established Scottish pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to howl or wail, especially in grief or celebration.

clue.text: Maybe one or two relatively dull

definitions.meaning: one and two are examples of numerals

explanation.surface: A couple of things, perhaps, that are fairly boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is pronounced NUM-er, the comparative of numb.
explanation.definitionFit: One and two are examples of numerals; separately, more numb means duller in feeling.

clue.text: Island prince imprisoned by Persian king

indicators.note: being imprisoned means being held inside, so the prince's letter sits within the king

parts.note: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian Achaemenid empire

explanation.surface: An island where a prince was locked up by an ancient Persian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a large island in the eastern Mediterranean.
